title: One Skill Too Many: How Co-Installed Skills Conflict in Coding Agents
title_zh: 技能太多反而冲突：编码智能体中共安装技能的冲突问题
abstract_en: Coding agents are extended with agent skills, directories whose SKILL.md tells the model when and how to perform a task. Because skills come from independent sources (teams, developers, plugins, copied collections), an installed skill can be co-installed with a similar skill doing the same job, and the model picks between them by name and description alone. In a conflict, the installed skill loses core functions (e.g., a ban on touching git) because the similar skill runs instead or changes what it does. The task still passes, so benchmarks that check only task completion miss such cases. We present the first empirical study of such conflicts. From snapshots of 20,947 repositories, we mine 822,109 candidate similar-skill pairs, have an LLM judge a stratified sample of 3,754, and run 312 confirmed pairs on three models (6,368 runs, 169,294 tool calls, 542 agent-hours). We report five findings. (1) Conflict-prone skills are common: nearly one in four installed skills is co-installed with one that does the same job, and 37% of judged skills sit inside copied collections. (2) Most such pairs involve normative skills, then capability skills. (3) Without lowering task completion, a similar skill takes one in five runs from the installed skill, and runs that open the similar skill first lose over a third of the exclusive core functions that only the installed skill fulfills. (4) Install location decides which skill runs, listing order barely matters, and the final reply names the skill used in only 0.9% of substituted runs. (5) Conflicts are decided at the first skill read, almost always before any file is changed, and a pre-tool hook at that read restores fidelity on exclusive core functions to the level of runs that open the installed skill first. Benchmarks should thus score exclusive core functions, and platforms should guard the first read and show which skill ran.
abstract_zh: Coding agent 可通过 agent skill 扩展能力；每个 skill 的 SKILL.md 会告诉模型何时以及如何执行任务。由于技能来自不同团队、开发者、插件和复制集合，功能相近的技能可能被同时安装，而模型仅凭名称和描述进行选择。当发生冲突时，模型可能改用相似技能，导致原安装技能的核心功能丢失，例如原技能禁止修改 git，但替代技能却执行了相关操作。任务仍可能成功，因此只检查任务完成度的 benchmark 会漏检此类问题。本文开展了首个关于该冲突的实证研究：从 20,947 个 repository 快照中挖掘出 822,109 对候选相似技能，由 LLM 对分层抽样的 3,754 对进行判断，并在 3 个模型上运行 312 对已确认冲突，共计 6,368 次运行、169,294 次工具调用和 542 个 agent-hours。研究发现：近四分之一的已安装技能会与执行相同任务的技能共存，37% 的受评技能位于复制集合中；冲突对主要涉及规范型技能，其次是能力型技能；在不降低任务完成率的情况下，相似技能约在五分之一的运行中取代已安装技能，且若模型先打开相似技能，已安装技能独有的核心功能会损失三分之一以上；安装位置决定最终运行哪个技能，而列表顺序影响很小，最终回复仅在 0.9% 的替代运行中说明实际使用的技能；冲突通常在首次读取技能时决定，且几乎总发生在修改文件之前。在首次读取处加入 pre-tool hook，可将独有核心功能的保真度恢复到先读取已安装技能时的水平。论文据此建议 benchmark 评估独有核心功能，平台保护首次读取行为并显示实际运行的技能。
key_points_zh: 共安装相似技能十分普遍：近四分之一的技能与同职能技能共存，37%的受评技能来自复制集合。
相似技能约在五分之一的运行中取代目标技能，但任务完成率通常不受影响，因此传统 benchmark 容易漏检。
若模型先读取相似技能，目标技能独有的核心功能会损失三分之一以上；安装位置比列表顺序更能决定技能选择。
冲突几乎在首次读取技能时、文件修改前就已确定；最终回复仅在0.9%的替代运行中说明实际使用的技能。
在首次读取处加入 pre-tool hook 可恢复功能保真度，平台应保护首次读取并显示实际运行的技能。

llm_assessment.comment: Although it does not evolve skills, this large empirical study exposes a consequential coding-agent skill-composition failure and provides an actionable runtime guard.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: 尽管该工作不涉及技能演化，但其大规模实证研究揭示了重要的编程智能体技能冲突，并给出了可操作的运行时防护机制。
